workflow.title: Verification without exposing medical data

steps.title: Medical order issued
steps.description: A doctor creates a medical test order inside their system. A cryptographic hash of the document is registered on blockchain.

steps.title: Patient authorizes laboratory access
steps.description: The patient grants the laboratory permission to view the order. Authorization can occur via QR code or one-click approval.

steps.title: Laboratory performs the test
steps.description: The laboratory updates the exam status and uploads the results. The new document is linked to the original order.

steps.title: Doctor verifies results
steps.description: The patient returns to the medical center. The doctor verifies the results instantly through HealthProof.

workflow.tagline: The patient does not share data.

techSections.decentralizedDesc: A distributed network where every participant is a peer. If one node goes offline, the rest of the network continues to operate without interruption.
techSections.clickNodeToSimulate: Click any node to simulate failure
techSections.noSinglePointDesc: There is no central server that can fail or be compromised. The network stays operational even when individual nodes disconnect.
techSections.resilienceDesc: Data and permissions are replicated across the network. If a hospital system goes down, patients can still access their records from any other verified node.
techSections.interoperabilityDesc: Different institutions, software vendors, and countries can all connect to the same network without needing custom integrations.
techSections.encryptionDesc: Every document is encrypted with a unique key that only the patient and authorized parties can unlock. Not even the platform operator can read the content.
techSections.encryptionIdle: Click a stage to see how encryption works.
techSections.keygenDesc: An ECDH P-256 key pair is generated in the browser. The private key never leaves the device.
techSections.encryptDesc: The document is encrypted with AES-GCM-256 using a unique session key derived from the recipient's public key.
techSections.transmitDesc: Only the encrypted payload and initialization vector travel over the network. The decryption key is derived locally.
techSections.decryptDesc: The recipient uses their private key to unwrap the session key and decrypt the document. Integrity is verified automatically.
techSections.traceabilityDesc: Every operation—creating an order, granting permission, uploading a result—is cryptographically signed and permanently recorded.

fhirReview.consentTitle: How should this document be processed?
fhirReview.consentBody: You can let AI extract and classify the results, or fill them in yourself without sending the document to external processors.

lab.consentTitle: How do you want to process this lab report?
lab.consentBody: AI will extract the lab tests, values, units, and reference ranges to generate a FHIR bundle.
lab.consentAiItem1: OCR runs locally in your browser using Tesseract.js; the document/image is NOT sent to OpenAI.
lab.consentAiItem2: Personal data (RUT, name, birth date) is detected and replaced locally with placeholders before sending text to OpenAI.
lab.consentAiItem3: OpenAI only receives anonymized text to identify lab tests, values, and generate the FHIR bundle. Placeholders are replaced with real data on your device right before publishing.
lab.consentAiItem4: HealthProof does not store raw text or the original document in its database. Only the FHIR bundle and the encrypted PDF on IPFS are kept.

obstetric.consentTitle: How do you want to process this obstetric ultrasound?
obstetric.consentBody: AI will extract fetal measurements (BPD, HC, AC, FL), gestational age, amniotic fluid, and placenta to generate a FHIR bundle.
obstetric.consentAiTitle: When using AI for obstetric ultrasound
obstetric.consentAiItem1: OCR runs locally in your browser using Tesseract.js; the document/image is NOT sent to OpenAI.
obstetric.consentAiItem2: Personal data (RUT, name, birth date) is detected and replaced locally with placeholders before sending text to OpenAI.
obstetric.consentAiItem3: OpenAI only receives anonymized text to identify fetal measurements, gestational age, and generate the FHIR bundle. Placeholders are replaced with real data on your device right before publishing.
obstetric.consentAiItem4: HealthProof does not store raw text or the original document in its database. Only the FHIR bundle and the encrypted PDF on IPFS are kept.

imaging.consentTitle: How do you want to process this abdominal ultrasound?
imaging.consentBody: AI will extract abdominal organ measurements (kidney, liver, spleen, gallbladder, bladder), findings, and diagnostic impression to generate a FHIR bundle.
imaging.consentAiTitle: When using AI for abdominal ultrasound
imaging.consentAiItem1: OCR runs locally in your browser using Tesseract.js; the document/image is NOT sent to OpenAI.
imaging.consentAiItem2: Personal data (RUT, name, birth date) is detected and replaced locally with placeholders before sending text to OpenAI.
imaging.consentAiItem3: OpenAI only receives anonymized text to identify abdominal measurements, anatomical regions, and generate the FHIR bundle. Placeholders are replaced with real data on your device right before publishing.
imaging.consentAiItem4: HealthProof does not store raw text or the original document in its database. Only the FHIR bundle and the encrypted PDF on IPFS are kept.

fhirReview.consentAiItem1: OCR runs locally in your browser using Tesseract.js; the document/image is NOT sent to OpenAI.
fhirReview.consentAiItem2: Personal data (RUT, name, birth date) is detected and replaced locally with placeholders before sending text to OpenAI.
fhirReview.consentAiItem3: OpenAI only receives anonymized text to identify exams, values, and generate the FHIR bundle. Placeholders are replaced with real data on your device right before publishing.
fhirReview.consentAiItem4: HealthProof does not store raw text or the original document in its database. Only the FHIR bundle and the encrypted PDF on IPFS are kept.
fhirReview.consentManualItem1: Neither the document nor any image is sent to external AI processors: you enter the data directly.
fhirReview.consentManualItem2: The form uses local validation to structure the information as a valid FHIR bundle.
fhirReview.consentManualItem3: You can fill in only the available data; fields that do not apply are marked N/A and omitted from the bundle.
fhirReview.scoreTooltip: The score measures the percentage of required fields (Must Support) from the CL-Core/CLIPS guide present in the bundle. To increase it, complete unit, method, reference range, and interpretation. Qualitative results (e.g., 'NON-REACTIVE') usually score lower because they use valueString instead of valueQuantity + unit.
fhirReview.scoreNotPerfect: The bundle is at {score}%. You can publish it as is, or go back and complete the missing fields to raise the score before publishing.
fhirReview.step1Hint: Confirm or correct the LOINC code for each exam
fhirReview.step2Hint: Complete the required data the AI did not detect
fhirReview.missingCount: {count, plural, =0 {All fields present} one {1 field to review} other {# fields to review}}
fhirReview.missingHint: Required data the AI did not detect

fieldHelp.unit: Indicates the unit of measurement for the result (e.g., mg/dL, U/L, mmol/L). FHIR uses this in Observation.valueQuantity.unit so the result is comparable.
fieldHelp.method: Describes the analytical technique used (e.g., chemiluminescence, enzymatic, immunofluorescence). FHIR records this in Observation.method to provide context for the result.
fieldHelp.referenceRange: The range of values considered normal for this test (e.g., 70-110 mg/dL). FHIR stores this in Observation.referenceRange to interpret whether the result is normal or abnormal.
fieldHelp.interpretation: Clinical interpretation of the result (e.g., normal, low, high). FHIR stores this in Observation.interpretation using the standard v3 code system.

fhirReview.noMissingFields: No required fields are missing. You can generate the FHIR bundle.
fhirReview.tourExamsDesc: Here you see each exam the AI found in the document. Check that the name, value, and LOINC are correct.
fhirReview.tourMissingDesc: The AI could not identify these required fields (unit, method, or reference range). Fill them in so the FHIR bundle is valid.
fhirReview.tourGenerateDesc: When everything looks correct, press this button to generate the FHIR bundle and continue.
fhirReview.previewLocalNote: Local preview: real personal data is reinserted on this device before publishing. The AI only processed the anonymized version.

imagingReview.loincApiFailedDesc: Could not reach the LOINC API. Showing codes from the local subset; please verify them before publishing.
